newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - June 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - June 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ministerial committee for privatisation has approved at its meeting on Monday the sale of 40 percent of Alexandria Flour Mills and 90 percent of Simo/Middle East Paper through the stock market within the next two weeks. Shares of the two firms will be offered at an initial price of 75 and 20 pounds ($22 and 5.9) respectively.

- A public offer to sell 10 percent of Upper Egypt Contracting was oversubscribed 73 times. The holding company National for Construction and Development raised the offered stake to 75 percent from 10 percent initially offered. The price was fixed through the price discovery system at 38.5 pounds per share.

- Suez Cement 's net after-tax profits were down to 240 million pounds ($70.7 million) in 1996 against 281.7 million pounds in the previous year. Chairman Mahmoud el-Khouli said the expiration of tax exemption for the firm's second plant and the finance of expansion projects were the reasons behind the decline in profits.

- Amriyah Cement profits rose to 143.33 million pounds in the first ten months of the 1996/7 financial year up to the end of April against 123.72 million in the same period last year. The firm is still enjoying a tax exemption that will be left by the end of 1998. The fiscal year begins on July 1.
- The general assembly of Misr International Bank/MIBANK decided to distribute 15 pound dividend per share for the year 1996.
- National Cement (Kawmia) 's made a net loss in the first nine months of 1996/7 financial year of 34.36 million pounds compared to 23.5 million in the same period last year.

- The general assembly of National Bank for Development/NBD agreed at its extraordinary meeting to increse the bank's issued capital to 200 million pounds from 150.6 million. The bank made 30.9 million pounds of profits in 1996 against 24.7 million in the previous year.

- Shams Housing and Development forecast 15 million pounds of profits in 1997/98. The firm made 16 million pounds of pre-tax profits in the first nine months of this year against a forecast of 9.8 million for the whole year.
